case_name: Smt. Krishna Veni v. The Union of India and others

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Krishna Veni, second wife of Sardar Natha Singh (since deceased)
parties.respondent_defendant: The Union of India and others

facts_of_case: Petitioner claimed widow pension under the Swatantra Sainik Samman Pension Scheme, 1980. Refused by Assistant Secretary to the Government of West Bengal on ground that deed of divorce was not acceptable under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A custom, to be upheld, is to be pleaded and proved by the party relying on it.
legal_principles.held: Learned counsel relies on Subramani and others vs. M. Chandralekha, reported at (2005) 9 SCC 407, for the proposition that a custom, to be upheld, is to be pleaded and proved by the party relying on the same.
cited_cases: Subramani and others vs. M. Chandralekha, (2005) 9 SCC 407

legal_principles.principle: The burden and initial onus lies on the party to prove the existence of a custom having the force of law.
legal_principles.held: The burden and initial onus lies on the petitioner to prove the existence of a custom having the force of law, to be proved by evidence - oral or documentary - in order to attract the benefit of Section 29(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: A decree of divorce can only be passed by a competent court on any of the grounds as mentioned in Section 13 of the Act.
legal_principles.held: The marriage between the respondent no.11 and her deceased husband could only be dissolved by a decree of divorce passed by a competent court on any of the grounds as mentioned in Section 13 of the Act, unless the existence of any contrary custom was proved by evidence.

legal_principles.principle: The respondent-authorities do not have the jurisdiction in law to decide the matrimonial status of private parties.
legal_principles.held: Unfortunately, neither does the writ court, with its constraints in taking evidence on disputed questions of fact, has the scope to decide such issue.

outcome.final_order: Petitioner is entitled to widow pension under the Swatantra Sainik Samman Pension Scheme, 1980.

keywords: Assistant Secretary to the Government of West Bengal
use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce pension
